title: COVID-19 Infections within Residential Healthcare Facilities
what_it_is: COVID-19 Infections within Residential Healthcare Facilities

sections.label: Reported COVID-19 cases in hospitals, nursing homes
sections.summary: From April to September 2022, about 330 hospital cluster cases and 3,000 nursing home cases were reported, under 1% of community cases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: From 1 April 2022 to 30 September 2022, there were around 330 reported cases from COVID-19 clusters in hospitals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Over the same period, around 3,000 COVID-19 cases were reported by the nursing homes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: These constitute a small proportion – less than 1% – of total reported community cases.

sections.label: Vaccination, severe illness, case fatality rate
sections.summary: COVID-19 vaccination cannot completely stop infections but prevents severe illness; over 90% of eligible nursing home residents were vaccinated, keeping Singapore's case fatality rate about 0.1%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: It cannot completely stop infections but is very effective in preventing severe illness from COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: We have provided COVID-19 vaccinations to over 90% of eligible nursing home residents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: With these measures, we have kept Singapore’s overall case fatality rate at about 0.1%, well below the global average of around 1%.

sections.label: Modelling transmission, clusters, spread; estimate
sections.summary: Modelling allowed scientists to study COVID-19 transmission and spread, and the 330 versus 3,000 figures may be an under-estimate but are approximately correct.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: This has allowed us and the scientists in our system to model the transmission and the clusters and the spread of COVID-19 within different settings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, to answer the question, yes, it may be an under-estimate, but I think we are confident that we have a robust handle on the relative proportions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, it is approximately correct – 330 versus 3,000.

sections.label: No data; file separate question
sections.summary: The speaker does not have the data and encourages the Member to file a separate question for further information.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: I do not have the data in front of me.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: I would encourage the Member to file a separate question if she would like further information on that.
